was among the first independent integrators to build grid-scale storage at scale,and for several years that position was the investment case," analyst Dimple Gosai wrote. "In 2021 and 2022, when cell supply was tight and most Western buyers had no relationships with Chinese manufacturers, the ability to source, integrate, and warrant a system was itself the value added, and Fluence was paid for it. The question for us is whether that value added still commands a price when cells are abundant, integration is widely replicated, and the largest suppliers manufacture their own cells."

Global BESS installations topped 320 GWh in 2025, up more than 50% Y/Y, while BloombergNEF pegged average turnkey BESS system prices at $117/kWh, a 31% Y/Y decline that Gosai said reflects Chinese cell-manufacturing overcapacity and intense competition.
"Cheap, abundant cells are the macro backdrop, and in our view, they compete away the procurement and integration role Fluence was originally paid for," the analyst said.

Gosai modeled FY 2027 and 2028 estimated EBITDA margins of 1.2%-3.3% vs. Wall Street consensus of 3%-4%, adding that declining order pricing and execution risk should pressure cash, as project delays and cost overruns raise working capital needs ahead of revenue conversion.

Liquidity is already down 32% Y/Y, and management has flagged $300M-$500M of additional working capital to support the order book over the next year, which the analyst said poses the risk of a dilutive equity raise due to constrained liquidity.
